The A11y Project checklist — digest (extract)
The checklist is a practical, step-by-step guide to auditing a web
project.

Content:
- Use plain language and avoid figures of speech, idioms, complex
  metaphors and culturally specific terms where possible.
- Provide alt text on functional images and images conveying
  information; leave decorative images empty.
- Avoid text on images; provide text alternatives for images used as
  links or buttons.
- Do not use colour alone to convey meaning.

Global code:
- Validate HTML; use a native element whenever possible (buttons,
  links, inputs).
- Keep heading levels in order; heading text is descriptive.
- Provide a unique and descriptive title per page.
- Use lang attribute on the html element.
- Rescue text with escaped entities; use semantic markup (strong/em).

Keyboard:
- All functionality is operable without a mouse: tab order matches
  reading order; visible focus indicator; no keyboard traps.

Forms:
- Labels are associated with controls and visible; error messages are
  associated with the field; autocomplete where useful.
- Required fields are clearly marked; errors are announced.

Media, animation, and motion:
- Provide transcripts for audio, captions for video; don't autoplay.
- Prefer prefers-reduced-motion support; no content that blinks more
  than 3 times, or that could cause seizures.
